kaps_punt: Beweging: gewerwelde diere kan beweeg, want daar is spiere wat vasgeheg is aan die skelet, gewrigte tussen die bene

items.bewering: 'n Dier se geraamte kan nie vanself beweeg nie. Bene is hard en styf en kan nie self skuif nie.
items.bron: Britannica, vertebrate (summary), https://www.britannica.com/summary/vertebrate: the skeleton is moved by muscles attached to bone or cartilage; Let's Talk Science, Musculoskeletal Systems in the Animal Kingdom, https://letstalkscience.ca/educational-resources/backgrounders/musculoskeletal-systems-in-animal-kingdom: muscles and bones work together to produce movement.

items.bewering: Baie van die dier se spiere is aan sy geraamte vasgeheg. Daardie spiere doen die werk en laat die bene beweeg.
items.bron: Britannica, vertebrate (summary), https://www.britannica.com/summary/vertebrate: 'The muscular system consists primarily of bilaterally paired masses attached to bones or cartilage.' 'Baie' is correctly limited, since heart and gut muscle are not attached to the skeleton.

items.bewering: Sonder spiere sou selfs die sterkste dier se geraamte doodstil bly lê.
items.bron: Same sources as above (Britannica vertebrate summary; Let's Talk Science). 'Die sterkste dier' is hypothetical and names no animal, so there is no ranking to check. The point holds: a skeleton has no means of moving itself, and an animal's strength sits in its muscles.

items.bewering: 'n Spier word korter en dikker wanneer hy 'n been laat beweeg. Dan trek hy aan die been waaraan hy vasgeheg is.
items.bron: USC Dornsife, 'What makes muscles contract? A physiologist explains how muscles move', https://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/what-makes-muscles-contract-physiologist-explains-how-muscles-move/ (a fibre gets shorter and pulls); on the thickening, PMC review of muscle shape change, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3289422: 'As a muscle shortens, it must increase in girth or cross-sectional area in order to maintain its volume.'

items.bewering: 'n Spier kan net trek, en hy kan nooit stoot nie.
items.bron: USC Dornsife (physiologist's explainer), https://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/what-makes-muscles-contract-physiologist-explains-how-muscles-move/: myosin only pulls and never pushes, which is why muscles work in opposing pairs. The absolute 'nooit' is the accepted statement for skeletal muscle and matches this lesson's context.

items.bewering: Buig jou arm en voel met jou ander hand aan die voorkant van jou boarm. Die spier daar word hard en bult op terwyl jou arm opkom.
items.bron: USC Dornsife, https://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/what-makes-muscles-contract-physiologist-explains-how-muscles-move/: the biceps on the front/inside of the upper arm shortens to bend the elbow; bulging from the constant-volume principle, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3289422.

items.bewering: 'n Gewrig is die plek waar twee of meer stewige dele van 'n geraamte bymekaar kom.
items.bron: Taber's Medical Dictionary, 'joint', https://nursing.unboundmedicine.com/nursingcentral/view/Tabers-Dictionary/740178/all/joint, and LibreTexts (James Madison University), Fibrous Joints, https://med.libretexts.org/Courses/James_Madison_University/A_and_P_for_STEM_Educators/06%3A_Joints/6.02%3A_Fibrous_Joints/6.2A%3A_Fibrous_Joints: a joint is where two or more bones (or bone and cartilage) meet. 'Stewige dele' covers both bone and cartilage correctly.

items.bewering: By baie van hierdie gewrigte kan die bene beweeg. Jou elmboog is so 'n gewrig, en jou arm kan daar buig en strek.
items.bron: CrossFit Essentials, Bones of the Elbow, https://www.crossfit.com/essentials/bones-of-the-elbow: the humeroulnar and humeroradial joints are hinge joints for bending and straightening; joints are classed as immovable, slightly movable or freely movable (Taber's / LibreTexts, above).

items.bewering: By daardie een gewrig kom daar selfs drie bene bymekaar.
items.bron: CrossFit Essentials, Bones of the Elbow, https://www.crossfit.com/essentials/bones-of-the-elbow: the elbow is formed by the humerus, ulna and radius.

items.bewering: Nie elke gewrig laat die bene so maklik beweeg nie. Die gewrigte tussen die bene bo-op 'n mens se kop beweeg byvoorbeeld amper glad nie.
items.bron: LibreTexts (James Madison University), Fibrous Joints, https://med.libretexts.org/Courses/James_Madison_University/A_and_P_for_STEM_Educators/06%3A_Joints/6.02%3A_Fibrous_Joints/6.2A%3A_Fibrous_Joints: cranial sutures are fibrous joints, immovable (synarthroses) in adults. 'Amper glad nie' is properly careful and allows for the slight give and the infant skull.

items.bewering: Spiere alleen kan nie 'n gewerwelde dier se arm of poot laat buig nie, en gewrigte alleen kan dit ook nie.
items.bron: Let's Talk Science, https://letstalkscience.ca/educational-resources/backgrounders/musculoskeletal-systems-in-animal-kingdom (muscles and bones together produce movement); USC Dornsife (muscles pull bones at joints), https://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/what-makes-muscles-contract-physiologist-explains-how-muscles-move/.

items.bewering: Stel jou 'n geraamte voor waarvan al die bene styf aan mekaar vassit. Die spiere kan so hard trek as wat hulle wil, en geen been skuif nie.
items.bron: Mapping checked against LibreTexts on fused/immovable joints, https://med.libretexts.org/Courses/James_Madison_University/A_and_P_for_STEM_Educators/06%3A_Joints/6.02%3A_Fibrous_Joints/6.2A%3A_Fibrous_Joints. The thought experiment maps soundly: where bones are fixed to each other (as in the adult skull, which the lesson has just named), nothing moves, so a learner reasoning on from it reaches the right conclusion: movement needs a movable joint. No faulty extension found.

items.bewering: Die gewrigte is die plekke waar die bene kan swaai wanneer 'n spier trek.
items.bron: CrossFit Essentials, https://www.crossfit.com/essentials/bones-of-the-elbow (hinge joints); USC Dornsife, https://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/what-makes-muscles-contract-physiologist-explains-how-muscles-move/ (a muscle pulls to bend the joint).

items.bewering: Byna elke gewerwelde dier gebruik dieselfde stelsel van geraamte, spiere en gewrigte.
items.bron: Britannica, vertebrate (summary), https://www.britannica.com/summary/vertebrate: a backbone, a skull and usually two pairs of limbs, with paired muscle masses attached to bone or cartilage; Britannica contributor page on the internal vertebrate skeleton, https://www.britannica.com/contributor/wd/1893. 'Byna elke' is weaker than the truth, not stronger, so it cannot be false.

items.bewering: 'n Mens loop deurdat spiere sy knie en sy heup by elke tree buig.
items.bron: OUHSC, Muscle activity during the gait cycle, https://ouhsc.edu/bserdac/dthompso/web/gait/kinetics/mmactsum.htm, and Wikipedia, Lower-limb walking pattern, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower-limb_walking_pattern: the hip and knee flex in every gait cycle, and the hip flexors (iliopsoas) start the swing. Part of the knee bend in the swing comes from the momentum of the hip action rather than from knee muscles, but the movement is still driven by muscles, so the sentence holds at this level.

items.bewering: 'n Voël vlieg met sterk borsspiere wat sy vlerke af en op trek.
items.bron: eLife reviewed preprint on dove flight muscles, https://elifesciences.org/reviewed-preprints/89968, and British Ornithologists' Union summary, https://bou.org.uk/?p=23723: the pectoralis (large breast muscle) pulls the wing down and the supracoracoideus, also a breast muscle lying under the pectoralis, pulls it up by a tendon running over the shoulder like a pulley. So 'af en op' by breast muscles is correct for both strokes, and it is accurate that the muscle that lifts the wing is also a breast muscle.

items.bewering: 'n Vis swem deurdat spiere langs sy ruggraat sy stert heen en weer swaai.
items.bron: Rhodes University ichthyology, Anatomy Lecture 4, https://www.ru.ac.za/media/rhodesuniversity/content/ichthyology/documents/Anatomy_Lecture_4.pdf, and PMC, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3130444: muscle segments (myomeres) attached to the vertebrae contract one after the other down each side and bend the body and tail from side to side. Some fish (e.g. seahorses) swim mainly with fins, but the generic sentence describes the usual way.

items.bewering: 'n Padda spring wanneer die spiere in sy lang agterpote skielik trek.
items.bron: PMC, In vivo muscle force and muscle power during near-maximal frog jumps, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5345813/: the jump is powered by hind-leg muscles (plantaris), and the whole push-off takes about a fifth of a second. The research adds that a tendon helps by storing and releasing energy, and this is still debated, but that detail does not make 'skielik trek' false at this level.

items.bewering: 'n Slang het geen pote nie en gly met spiere langs sy hele ruggraat.
items.bron: Smithsonian's National Zoo, How Do Snakes Move Without Legs?, https://nationalzoo.si.edu/news/news/how-do-snakes-move-without-legs: around 175 to 400 vertebrae and ribs linked by 10 000 to 15 000 muscles, working in groups along the body. Some pythons and boas keep tiny spurs left over from hind legs, but these are not legs, so 'geen pote nie' stands.

items.bewering: spier: "'n Deel van die lyf wat korter word en trek."
items.bron: USC Dornsife, https://dornsife.usc.edu/news/stories/what-makes-muscles-contract-physiologist-explains-how-muscles-move/: muscle fibres shorten and pull. Read alone, the entry is true of every kind of muscle.

items.bewering: gewrig: "Die plek waar twee of meer stewige dele van 'n geraamte bymekaar kom."
items.bron: Taber's Medical Dictionary, 'joint', https://nursing.unboundmedicine.com/nursingcentral/view/Tabers-Dictionary/740178/all/joint. Matches the study block's sentence word for word. Read alone it is true: it does not claim that every joint moves.

items.bewering: geraamte: "Die stewige dele wat 'n dier se lyf ophou en sy sagte dele beskerm."
items.bron: Let's Talk Science, Musculoskeletal Systems in the Animal Kingdom, https://letstalkscience.ca/educational-resources/backgrounders/musculoskeletal-systems-in-animal-kingdom, and Britannica vertebrate summary, https://www.britannica.com/summary/vertebrate: a skeleton supports the body and protects organs (e.g. skull, ribcage). Read alone the entry is true and fits both inner skeletons and shells. It leaves out movement and does not claim every animal has hard parts.

opsomming: All 22 claims hold up against sources. The muscle lesson is correct throughout, including that a bird's wing is lifted by a breast muscle as well as pulled down by one, and the fused-skeleton thought experiment leads a learner to the right conclusion, so nothing needs to change.
